references.text: Moses emphasizes that sacrifice and worship must take place at the place the Lord chooses, not anywhere in Israel. This establishes the principle of one central place of worship.
The warning against offering burnt offerings anywhere, and the command to offer them only at the place the Lord chooses within one of the tribes.
The Passover sacrifice is to be slaughtered at the place the Lord chooses for His name to dwell there.
The continuation of the verse specifying that the Passover must be sacrificed at the place the Lord chooses, at sunset.
The original Passover ordinance where the lamb was slaughtered in homes, now changed to require centralized worship.
The Israelites celebrated the Passover at Gilgal after entering the Promised Land, in accordance with the command to celebrate it at the proper place.
King Hezekiah summoned all Israel to celebrate the Passover in Jerusalem, the place the Lord had chosen.
King Josiah celebrated the Passover in Jerusalem with strict adherence to the law of centralized worship.
